pr_body:
# Change incorrect usage of ArgumentNullException

## Description

Change some thrown exceptions from ArgumentNullException to ArgumentException.
Specifically also when it was thrown, if the argument was the empty string.

Fixes #23671

issue_context.title: ArgumentNullException is thrown when argument isn't null but empty
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Some methods throws ArgumentNullException when argument is not null but it's empty.

See https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/3817 for exapmles.

review_comments: This feels like an incorrect change since `token.Name` _is_ null here. It seems like what we want to do here is note that it is for `nameof(AuthenticationToken.Name)`?

Yes, a property of an element of 'tokens' is null. But the argument 'tokens' itself is not null. Strictly speaking the ArgumentNullException will hence be the wrong one, IMO.

However 'tokens' does not meet the parameter specification of the called method, as the remarks for ArgumentException says here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception?view=net-8.0

And trying to add the exception for the null property (which may not be what you hinted at) gives this problem, since 'Name' is not a parameter to the method: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/108188902/232574571-7d1c074e-1976-4955-a560-905c8bcd0f54.png)

Thanks for clarifying. This justification makes sense given that `token.Name` is not an argument to the method. I think the update to the exception message makes it a little clearer as to what is happening here.
